standard_prerequisites.name: No universal computable function
standard_prerequisites.use: The contradiction target: if h were computable, Un' would be a universal computable function for the total partial computable functions, contradicting the stub.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1370-1381): h(e,x) = 1 if Un(e,x) is defined, 0 otherwise, is not computable.
Reductio (proof lines 1383-1407): assume h computable; define Un'(e,x) = Un(e,x) if h(e,x)=1, else 0;
Un' is total and computable when h is: realised as g(h(e,x),e,x) with g built by primitive recursion (g(0,e,x)=0, g(y+1,e,x)=Un(e,x));
Un' agrees with Un wherever the latter is defined, so it is universal for the total partial computable functions - contradicting thm:no-univ.
proof_roadmap: Assume h computable and define the patched universal Un'.
Show Un' is total and computable via the primitive-recursive g composed with h.
Derive universality for total functions and contradict the no-universal theorem.
difficulty_reason: Undecidability of the halting problem (statement 1370-1381, proof 1383-1407): a complete reductio whose computability realisation (primitive recursion + composition with h) is written out. H2.
